text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Acting parliament speaker Khoury calls the 128 MPs to meet next Tuesday to elect a speaker for the new parliament.

-The spiritual leader of Lebanon's pro-Iranian Moslem militants Sheikh Fadlallah says the Islamic Resitance has gained politically by not responding with Katyusha rockets to Israel's bombardment of a south Lebanon village last week in which 10 civilians were wounded.
-The Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rise by $96.9 million in the first two weeks of October.
-The killer of the head of a police station in the Shouf mountains to be executed today by firing squad at Roumyeh jail.
-Prime Minister Hariri arrives in Washington and meets with President Clinton tomorrow.
-Israeli jets stage mock raids over Nabatiyeh and Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge which is controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas.
-A new government made up of a majority of MPs to be headed by Hariri may be formed.
-Speaker of the outgoing parliament Berri met with Syrian President Assad for three hours in Damascus.
-Washington to tell Hariri: Security in Lebanon is not sufficient and the ban on the travel of Americans to Beirut to continue.
